tonight.headline: Nothing to do in Chem today either, and for the second run running that is the honest answer rather than a thin one.
body: Week 2 has not kicked off. Your first lock is Josh Allen on Thursday at 18:15 Mexico City. ESPN has you 126.2 to Panda Attack's 124.8 and prices it 51%, which on a 1.4-point gap is noise and nothing here acts on it.

Your lineup is already the optimal one on this snapshot - I recomputed it rather than assuming. McLaurin holds the flex over Jalen Coker by 0.6 projected points, and Isaiah Likely holds tight end over Kyle Pitts by 0.4. Both of those gaps are inside the noise, so both were decided on reporting instead, and both came out the same way they did yesterday - for better reasons than yesterday had.

The one thing that changed is structural and it is in What went wrong: this run finally fired at 07:00 Mexico City as scheduled, and that confirms the schedule itself is set six hours too late to ever influence a waiver run.

case.label: What decides the week
case.body: Panda Attack start Dak Prescott, Chase Brown, Saquon Barkley, Javonte Williams in the flex, George Pickens and Davante Adams. Three of those nine - Prescott, Pickens and Javonte Williams - are Dallas players hosting Washington, so their total is correlated: one Cowboys result moves a third of their lineup at once, in either direction. Yours is spread over six games with Allen on Thursday and Likely on Monday, so you will spend four days knowing more than they do about half your roster.

case.label: Where you are actually ahead
case.body: Josh Allen faces Detroit, 29th of 32 on FantasyPros' Week 2 board - the softest draw anyone on either roster has. Panda Attack's answer is Jalen Hurts at 20.1 projected, sitting on their bench, because Chem starts one quarterback. That is the single largest structural edge on the board and it is free.

case.label: The thing I could not price
case.body: Terry McLaurin. He is your flex and I could not retrieve a single current piece of Washington reporting for him this run - every McLaurin result that came back was from the 2025 season, including one Commanders injury page that reads like a live report and is not. His tile is graded on the Dallas matchup alone and his role is taken from the league file, not from reporting.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Panda Attack move Javonte Williams out of the flex for Jaylen Waddle, or Dallas and Washington produce the shootout their 19th and 27th ranked defences point at - either way the correlation runs their way instead of against them. Also falsified if Coker practises fully and McLaurin appears on Washington's Wednesday report, which would flip the flex on the reporting rather than on the 0.6 points.

whatWentWrong.title: The schedule is set six hours too late to ever affect a waiver run, and this morning proved it rather than fixing it.
whatWentWrong.lead: Yesterday's brief blamed the clock for firing at 07:40 UTC instead of 13:00. It fired at 13:05 UTC today - exactly 07:05 Mexico City, exactly as configured - and the claims were still settled six hours before it started.

case.label: The arithmetic nobody has done
case.body: Chem processes waivers at 07:00 UTC. That is 01:00 Mexico City. A brief scheduled for 07:00 Mexico City is 13:00 UTC and therefore lands six hours after every claim has already run, every single day, forever. Yesterday's diagnosis - that the task fired at the wrong hour - was wrong. The task fired at the right hour and the right hour is the wrong hour.

case.label: What it costs, concretely
case.body: Today the wire holds Mark Andrews at 82.2% rostered, Brock Purdy at 87.2%, Bo Nix at 85.1%, Jakobi Meyers at 78.2% and Xavier Worthy at 73.0%, all as free agents in a ten-team league. None of them needed a claim. But the three genuine claims that did run - Stafford, Jordan Addison, Makai Lemon clearing Thursday at 07:00 UTC - will resolve at 01:00 Mexico City tomorrow, again before any brief sees them.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Moving this task to roughly 06:00 UTC - midnight Mexico City - which is after the overnight reporting lands and before waivers process. That is the only change that converts this from a post-mortem into a decision tool on waiver days. Until then, every Chem waiver decision is being made by Hans without a brief, and the brief should stop pretending otherwise.

whatWentWrong.sources: ESPN activity log · ESPN league settings

whatWentWrong.title: Kyle Pitts cannot score for you in this league unless Isaiah Likely gets hurt, and yesterday's brief held him without saying so.
whatWentWrong.lead: Chem's flex is RB/WR only - slot 3. Pitts is a tight end. With Likely healthy and rostered, Pitts's 11.3 projected points are structurally unreachable, not merely benched.

case.label: The structural fact
case.body: Your lineup has exactly one tight-end slot and a flex that excludes tight ends. That is a Chem-specific rule - IPADE's flex at slot 23 does take a tight end, which is why the same problem does not exist there. Yesterday's brief listed Pitts as 'held in writing this morning' among droppable seats without naming the reason he is the most droppable of them.

case.label: Why his case got worse this run, not better
case.body: Atlanta's quarterback is Cooper Rush after what FOX Sports called a shaky effort in an opening loss to Pittsburgh. Tua Tagovailoa strained an oblique in practice on 10 September and his Week 2 practice participation is still listed TBD. Michael Penix Jr. is targeting a Week 2 or Week 3 debut off a knee and carries a QUESTIONABLE tag at 1.3% rostered. Three quarterbacks, no answer, and Pitts is the pass-catcher downstream of all of it.

case.label: Why he is still not a card
case.body: Because dropping a 94.3%-rostered player needs a better landing spot than this wire offers, and because Pitts is your only insurance at a required position. Likely plays Monday night - the last game of your week - so if Likely is ruled out you will find out far too late to claim a replacement. That insurance is what the 94.3% is buying and it is worth more than Romeo Doubs.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Atlanta naming Penix or Tua as the Week 2 starter, which makes Pitts startable somewhere and worth keeping on merit; or Likely clearing 8 targets again on Monday, which retires the insurance argument and makes Pitts the drop for the best available receiver. Either resolution ends the ambiguity this row exists to name.

worthALook.name: Romeo Doubs
worthALook.lead: Carried over from yesterday and downgraded on today's reporting. He is not the priority pickup that column made him sound like.

case.label: What is real
case.body: A.J. Brown is on injured reserve and Athlon and Yahoo both put the absence at six games, not an open-ended stint. That is a genuine 90-target hole in a New England offence, it is free here at 59.7% rostered in a ten-team league, and Doubs already plays the snaps.

case.label: What yesterday's brief got wrong about him
case.body: It called him FantasyPros' priority Week 2 pickup and left it there. The reporting that actually exists is a three-way argument - Yahoo, NESN and The Big Lead are all running the same piece asking whether Mack Hollins, DeMario Douglas or Doubs leads New England, and SI's headline on Doubs is that he has a major opportunity to rebound from a shaky debut. Being one of three candidates on a bad offence is a materially thinner case than being the replacement.

case.label: Why he is a row and not a card
case.body: He would not start for you. Your receivers are Jefferson and Garrett Wilson and the flex is a live McLaurin-versus-Coker decision at 12.7 and 12.1. Doubs at 10.6 is behind both, and he costs a roster seat you would have to take from Pitts, who is your only tight-end insurance in a league whose flex cannot hold a tight end.

case.label: When to act
case.body: Doubs clearing eight targets in Week 2 while still unrostered here, or New England naming him the clear WR1 on the Friday report. Either turns a three-way split into a role. Hollins is also free at 3.0% rostered and I did not research him - if Doubs becomes the answer, check Hollins's number before assuming Doubs is the cheaper one.

worthALook.sources: Athlon · Yahoo Sports · NESN · Sports Illustrated · ESPN

worthALook.name: Mark Andrews
worthALook.lead: The loudest ownership anomaly on this wire - 82.2% rostered nationally, free here - and the reason he matters is Pitts, not Likely.

case.label: Why the row exists
case.body: This is the wire signal the runbook ranks highest: a player whose national roster share says he is a starter, sitting unrostered in a ten-team league. Nobody in Chem has claimed a top-16 tight end. He is a free agent, not a claim, so he costs a roster move and no waiver priority - which matters because you sit 10th of 10 in Chem priority even though it resets weekly.

case.label: The honest problem
case.body: He does not start over Likely, and Chem's flex cannot take a tight end, so adding him would simply move the structural dead seat from Pitts to Andrews. He is only interesting as a swap - Andrews in, Pitts out - and that trade is a question about which tight end you want as insurance, not an upgrade to your lineup. I did not research Andrews's Week 1 usage or Baltimore's tight-end split this run, so I am not making that call for you.

case.label: When to act
case.body: Likely ruled out for Monday night, which is the one event that makes a second tight end score points for you. Failing that, if you decide Pitts's Atlanta situation is unsalvageable, Andrews is the same seat with a settled quarterback and a defence facing New Orleans's 26th-ranked unit. Do the Andrews research before making that swap, not after.

doNotChase.name: 49ers D/ST
doNotChase.lead: 4th of 32 this week, the biggest ownership move on the whole wire at +28.01, a free agent - and still not worth the move.

case.label: Why the market moved
case.body: San Francisco's roster share rose 28.01 points in a day, more than three times any other name here. The reason is on the other side of the ball: Miami start Malik Willis in a declared rebuild under Jeff Hafley, and FantasyPros rank Miami 32nd of 32 as a defensive matchup, which is the same information pointing the other way. The whole market can see this at once, which is exactly why it is not an edge.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: Baltimore is 3rd on that board, San Francisco 4th. ESPN price them 7.6 and 7.8. You are being offered two tenths of a point to move a seat that changed hands 30 hours ago and three times in nine days. That is a roster move spent on rounding error.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Baltimore finishing outside the top 12 defensive scores in Week 2 while San Francisco finishes top 5. Then the seat is open on merit and the 49ers are first on the list. The clause is unchanged from yesterday and it has not fired.

doNotChase.name: Jordan Addison
doNotChase.lead: Still on waivers, still clearing Thursday 01:00 Mexico City, still the trap it was yesterday - and I did not re-research him, which you should know before acting on this row.

case.label: The standing argument
case.body: T.J. Hockenson was Minnesota's second target behind Justin Jefferson in Week 1 on an 81% route share, which puts Addison third at best. JuiceJam dropped him at 07:14 yesterday to claim Devaughn Vele - a manager with the same information preferring a 35%-owned New Orleans receiver. The 76.2% is a memory of what he was and the -2.96 daily move is the market correcting it.

case.label: What is new and what it does
case.body: The quarterback picture got worse, not better. Kyler Murray is in concussion protocol and described as highly questionable; Minnesota's replacement is disputed between Carson Wentz and Cam Ward depending on the source. A third receiver in an offence with an unsettled quarterback is not the shape you spend a Thursday claim on, even in a league where priority resets.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Murray clearing protocol and Addison drawing 7+ targets in Week 2, or Jefferson missing time. Be aware this row is carried forward on yesterday's research plus today's quarterback reporting - I ran no Addison-specific search this run, and the RotoBaller column yesterday's brief cited was never retrievable beyond its headline.

He is 0.6 projected points from taking the flex off McLaurin.

settled.title: Start Isaiah Likely over Kyle Pitts (14 September)
settled.result: Reaffirmed on a new fact. Likely caught Jaxson Dart's first touchdown pass of 2026 in the Giants' Week 1 win, and Theo Johnson's shoulder is still limiting him, so Likely's target share has no internal competition. Atlanta meanwhile still has three quarterbacks and no answer.

settled.title: Add Brian Thomas Jr. for Stefon Diggs (12 September)
settled.result: Holding, unchanged. Coach Liam Coen has him limited this week with the shoulder and expects him to play. Production still has not arrived at 3 for 40, and Denver at 8th of 32 is the hardest draw on your roster. Review after Week 3 as scheduled.

settled.title: Start Jaylen Warren over Bhayshul Tuten (13 September)
settled.result: Held. Warren was named the starter over Rico Dowdle for 2026 but took fewer snaps than Dowdle in Week 1; what saves it is 5 catches on 6 targets. Tuten is in a worse version of the same problem - fewer routes than his own backup. Different league, same lesson.

settled.title: Drop Kyle Monangai for Tre Tucker (13 September)
settled.result: Worse than it looked yesterday. Pro Football Network report Monangai and D'Andre Swift dominated Chicago's targets in the 59-37 win, so he is a receiving back in a 59-point offence, not just a returning knee. Still not startable over Warren; still never the drop.

settled.title: Withdraw the McLaurin + Stafford for DeVonta Smith offer (15 September)
settled.result: Retired and now impossible - Stafford was the drop in yesterday's Coker claim and is on the Chem wire on waivers. Recorded so no future run re-discovers it.

cannotSee.label: This brief cannot reach a Chem waiver run, by design
cannotSee.body: Chem processes at 07:00 UTC, which is 01:00 Mexico City. A 07:00 Mexico City task is 13:00 UTC and lands six hours late every day. Today's claims settled at 07:14 UTC and tomorrow's - Stafford, Jordan Addison, Makai Lemon, the Patriots and Jaguars defences, Chris Boswell - settle at 07:00 UTC Thursday, again before this task next runs. See What went wrong.

cannotSee.label: Wednesday's practice reports do not exist yet
cannotSee.body: It is 09:05 on the US East Coast. NFL teams practise Wednesday afternoon and the participation reports follow. Every injury read in this file - Coker's ankle, Brian Thomas Jr.'s shoulder, Kyler Murray's protocol, Tua's oblique - is Sunday-through-Tuesday information. Nothing from today's sessions is in here.

cannotSee.label: Terry McLaurin was not researched successfully and he is your flex
cannotSee.body: Every McLaurin result returned was from the 2025 season, including a Commanders page about a Lions game and one saying he and Jayden Daniels were both out against Atlanta - neither is current. I have no 2026 usage, target share or practice information for him at all. He holds the flex on a 0.6-point projection gap over Coker and on nothing else. This is the single weakest-supported starting decision in the file.

cannotSee.label: Two sources disagree about who replaces Kyler Murray and I picked one
cannotSee.body: FantasyPros on 14 September say Carson Wentz would start for Minnesota. DraftKings Network on 15 September say backup Cam Ward finished the game. The league file lists Wentz on Minnesota and Cam Ward on Tennessee, so I took Wentz on two-of-three. If DraftKings are right about the depth chart, Justin Jefferson's tile is built on the wrong quarterback.

cannotSee.label: The matchup grades are one board, read in one direction
cannotSee.body: Every tile comes from FantasyPros' Week 2 defense streaming board of 32, retrieved this run. It ranks defences as fantasy plays - sacks and turnovers - not as coverage against a specific position, and it is a weekly opinion piece rather than season data. Two weeks in, points allowed by position does not exist. Yesterday's brief used the same board and the numbers match, so the grades are at least stable.

cannotSee.label: Players named in this file that I did not research
cannotSee.body: Khalil Shakir, Xavier Worthy, Jakobi Meyers, Brock Purdy and Bo Nix are named only as evidence that the wire is blundered - I checked none of them and no recommendation rests on any of them. Mark Andrews has a watch row and his Week 1 usage was not researched; that row says so. Jordan Addison's doNotChase row is carried from yesterday plus today's quarterback reporting, with no Addison-specific search this run.

cannotSee.label: Three page fetches returned navigation only
cannotSee.body: NBC Sports' Week 2 injury report, RotoBaller's Week 2 waiver rankings, and The Falcoholic's Cooper Rush piece - the last blocked by robots.txt. The Atlanta quarterback picture is therefore built on DraftKings Network and a FOX Sports headline rather than on the Falcons beat piece I went looking for.

cannotSee.label: Several searches returned 2025 articles that read as current
cannotSee.body: A CBS piece on Brock Bowers dated 14 September 2025 describes a different injury under a different head coach; the current Raiders coach in these files is Kubiak, not Pete Carroll. A Baltimore Beatdown Lamar Jackson page describes a back contusion and a Saturday game against Green Bay, also 2025. I discarded both. This is the second consecutive run where a stale page nearly got used, and it is the main reason to distrust any fact here without a 2026 date attached.

cannotSee.label: The payload schema in the runbook does not match what the app reads
cannotSee.body: The runbook's Step 6 describes doFirst, trades, candidates and defense. The files actually published to this repository - and therefore what the app renders - use nine sections: tonight, doFirst, whatWentWrong, roster, trades, worthALook, doNotChase, settled, cannotSee. I wrote the nine-section shape because that is the live contract, and added candidates and defense alongside it so the runbook's validator has the fields it checks. Nothing was dropped; someone should reconcile the two documents.
